a76.speaker: Mary Beth Leonard, US Ambassador to the African Union
a76.speech: "The long history of trade ties between the United States and Africa pushed the US to further deepen trade with Africa," and added that the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is a real game changer for how international and US business looks at Africa because it has created significant opportunities.

a76.speaker: Florizelle Liser, President and CEO of the Corporate Council on Africa
a76.speech: Described the motivation to foster a better trade relationship with Africa: "We have a stake in supporting African regional integration, in creating larger markets and businesses, allowing them to take advantage of economies of scale and drawing Africa into regional and global value chains." ; "There are many positive things happening in Ethiopia and the export of products to the US market is an example to what Africa can do and is doing across the continent."

a76.speaker: Albert Muchanga, AU Trade and Industry Commissioner
a76.speech: Said work is underway to develop regional value and supply chains and to create a more stable and predictable policy framework to guide business investment and trading decisions in Africa, including advancing liberalization of trade in goods and services and establishing a payment and settlement platform. "Through the African Continental Free Trade Area, we are offering large economies of scale and scope to the private sector," adding that the continent's trade liberalization and integration gives incentives to invest in larger-scale, longer-term endeavors.

a134.speaker: Trump administration
a134.speech: Announced on Wednesday 26 February 2025 that it was making massive cuts to American international aid, in particular through the elimination of 92% of the funding of overseas programmes by USAID, boasting of “saving American taxpayers nearly 60 billion dollars”.

a134.speaker: Federal judge (US, unnamed)
a134.speech: Suspended the decision to freeze expenditure approved by Congress, after being seized by two organisations grouping together companies, NGOs and other beneficiaries of American aid funds.

a134.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a134.speech: Decided, following a review of these programmes carried out by his services, to definitively eliminate nearly 5,800 of the funding grants awarded around the world by the agency, with a remaining cost of 54 billion dollars, keeping only a little over 500, according to the State Department.

a134.speaker: Spokesperson for American diplomacy (US State Department, unnamed)
a134.speech: Specified that of more than 9,100 grants awarded by the State Department, for a total amount of 15.9 billion dollars, 4,100 – at an estimated cost of 4.4 billion – have been cancelled.

a134.speaker: US State Department
a134.speech: Assures that USAID is maintaining “vital” grants such as food assistance and treatments for patients suffering from AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria, as well as for countries such as Lebanon, Haiti, Venezuela and Cuba.

a134.speaker: USAID
a134.speech: Announced on 23 February 2025 the dismissal of 1,600 of its employees in the United States and the placement of the majority of its personnel on administrative leave.

a293.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a293.speech: Responded to the development by instructing Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson to address the funding gap created by the suspension of USAID's international funding programme ; expressed deep concern over the estimated $156 million funding shortfall, particularly the projected $78.2 million shortfall that would impact critical interventions such as malaria prevention, maternal and child health, and the fight against HIV/AIDS.

a293.speaker: Daily Graphic (editorial)
a293.speech: "The Daily Graphic takes the view that, as the country faces the potential loss of USAID funding, it is crucial to consider strategies for building resilience and fostering self-reliance." ; argues the suspension of funding should encourage Ghana to diversify its funding sources and explore public-private partnerships, strengthen domestic resource mobilisation to reduce dependence on external aid, invest in capacity-building to enhance local expertise and implementation capabilities, and leverage technology and innovation, so that Ghana can create a more resilient and self-reliant development model and accelerate the Ghana Beyond Aid agenda.

a314.speaker: Parents (speaking on The Closing Argument programme, 28 August 2025)
a314.speech: Said private schools charge more yet deliver less, and that many communities lack public options.

a314.speaker: Teachers from private schools (speaking on The Closing Argument programme)
a314.speech: Spoke about no professional development, low pay, and little attention to quality because oversight is weak.

a314.speaker: Dr. Chris Tokpah, Associate Vice President for Institutional Effectiveness at Delaware County Community College and co-owner of the Center for Research, Evaluation, and Policy (CENREP), author
a314.speech: Argued last year that Liberia should use WASSCE results to strengthen accountability with clearer reporting, and now recommends that every school - public, private or faith-based - receive a five-year license that must be earned back at renewal on the basis of WASSCE performance, with annual checkups, automatic probation after two consecutive years of zero passes, public school-level ranking and reporting, support before sanctions, fairness guardrails, and one national academic calendar with mandatory professional training days; adding that the Ministry must hold itself to the same standards it sets for private schools.

a314.speaker: Liberian elders (proverb cited by the author)
a314.speech: “Our elders told us that the one who points the way should first walk the path.”

a619.speaker: China-Africa Changsha Declaration on Upholding Solidarity and Cooperation of the Global South (issued at the FOCAC Ministerial Coordinator's meeting)
a619.speech: China and African countries sent out a strong message for solidarity and cooperation of the Global South through the Changsha Declaration, in the firm belief that countries should uphold true multilateralism, safeguard the UN-centred international system, defend the WTO-centred multilateral trading system and make economic globalisation more open, inclusive, mutually beneficial and balanced, so as to foster a better trade, investment and financing environment for the Global South.

a619.speaker: China (announcement at the FOCAC Ministerial Coordinator's meeting)
a619.speech: Announced that it will expand the zero-tariff treatment for 100 percent tariff lines to all 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with it, to help quality products from Africa access the Chinese market ; announced that for the least developed countries in Africa it will roll out further measures on market access, inspection and quarantine, and customs clearance to boost trade in goods, enhance skills and technical training, and expand the promotion of quality products.

a619.speaker: Han Jing, Chinese Ambassador to Zambia
a619.speech: Says he is pleased to see that the rise and growth of the Global South represents the unstoppable trend of our times and the future of development, in face of frequent occurrence of unilateralism, protectionism and economic bullying by a certain country for selfish gains ; says the international community should give prioritised attention to the economic difficulties and development challenges faced by African countries, and that development assistance to African countries should be increased, not unilaterally slashed, to provide continued support to help African countries improve people's livelihood, reduce poverty and boost economic and social development.

a619.speaker: Han Jing, Chinese Ambassador to Zambia
a619.speech: Says China and Zambia are all-weather friends and Comprehensive Strategic and Cooperative Partners, that in 2024 trade between China and Zambia reached $6.703 billion, a 26.5 percent year-on-year growth, with over 600 Chinese companies operating in Zambia and accumulative investment exceeding $3.8 billion, creating more than 30,000 local jobs ; says China will further assist in constructing milling plants and water supply projects, work with Zambia to establish a cholera vaccine manufacturing plant through a joint venture and provide medical supplies for HIV/AIDS response ; says negotiation for the TAZARA revitalisation is making good progress and the project is expected to be launched within this year ; says that no matter how the international situation evolves, China's door to Zambia and Africa will only open wider.

a670.speaker: Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, Egyptian President
a670.speech: Proposed on Sunday a two-day truce in the Gaza Strip to free hostages, proposing in Cairo "a two-day ceasefire during which four hostages would be exchanged for prisoners" held by Israel ; added that this would be a precondition before entering into "negotiations within ten days" aimed at "a complete ceasefire and the entry of humanitarian aid" into the besieged Palestinian territory.

a670.speaker: Massoud Pezeshkian, Iranian President
a670.speech: Said the Islamic Republic was not seeking war, but promised an "appropriate response" to the Israeli strikes, despite calls for restraint.

a670.speaker: Ali Khamenei, Iranian Supreme Leader
a670.speech: Said the strikes should be "neither exaggerated nor minimised."

a670.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a670.speech: Said the attack on Iran "achieved all its objectives" ; said the air force had struck "Iran's defence capabilities and its missile-manufacturing capabilities" aimed at Israel.

a670.speaker: Tehran (Iranian government)
a670.speech: Said the 1 October missile fire on Israel was intended to avenge Israel's assassination of Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah near Beirut and of Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran.

a670.speaker: Israel
a670.speech: Said the strikes were also a response to attacks by Iran-backed movements, in reference to Hezbollah and Hamas.

a670.speaker: Israeli army
a670.speech: Says its ground and air offensive in Jabalia since 6 October is intended to prevent Hamas from regrouping its forces ; has declared 34 of the remaining hostages dead ; said it had lost 37 soldiers in fighting against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

a670.speaker: Witnesses in northern Gaza
a670.speech: Reported strikes on Sunday, notably in Jabalia.

a670.speaker: Gaza Civil Defence
a670.speech: Said an Israeli strike on a school turned into a shelter for people displaced from Jabalia killed nine Palestinians near Gaza City.

a670.speaker: Palestinian Red Crescent
a670.speech: Said on Monday that an Israeli drone killed three people during a gathering east of Gaza City.

a670.speaker: AFP tally based on official Israeli data
a670.speech: Counts 1,206 people, mostly civilians, killed in the 7 October 2023 attack, including hostages killed or who died in captivity; of 251 people abducted, 97 remain hostages in Gaza ; an AFP tally based on official figures counts at least 1,620 people killed in Lebanon since 23 September.

a670.speaker: Hamas Health Ministry (Gaza)
a670.speech: Says at least 42,847 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed in the Israeli offensive, figures the UN considers reliable.

a670.speaker: United Nations
a670.speech: Considers the Gaza Health Ministry casualty data reliable.

a670.speaker: Official Lebanese news agency
a670.speech: Reported that an Israeli strike killed at least three people on Monday morning in the coastal city of Tyre.

a670.speaker: Lebanese Health Ministry
a670.speech: Said at least 21 people had been killed on Sunday in raids on Haret Saida, Ain Baal and Bourj al-Shemali.

a784.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a784.speech: Announced in a live address from the grounds of the Executive Mansion that Liberia had secured a second compact from the Millennium Challenge Corporation and celebrated the news as a testament to Liberia's progress in governance and reform: "According to the MCC, Liberia has qualified for a second compact due to our outstanding performance in governance and reform. This giant achievement will unlock resources for our development agenda and help address the binding constraints to growth in our country." ; "This is not just a victory for the government but for all Liberians. It reflects the international community's confidence in our ability to deliver progress through unity and reform. Let us join hands to celebrate this collective success."

a784.speaker: ArcelorMittal Liberia (company)
a784.speech: Joined in the celebrations, congratulating President Boakai and the Liberian people, and reaffirmed its long-term commitment to Liberia, highlighting the alignment between MCC's principles of economic growth and good governance and its own investment strategy.

a784.speaker: ArcelorMittal company official
a784.speech: "ArcelorMittal believes that economic growth is more effective at reducing poverty in well-governed countries."

a784.speaker: Unnamed senior official at ArcelorMittal Liberia (anonymous)
a784.speech: Noted the synergy between the compact and the company's investments: "If ArcelorMittal expands next year and with the MCC compact, coupled with the mining sector's growth, the country is expected to generate substantial government revenue through taxes and royalties and create much-needed jobs for Liberians." ; "Liberia's reliance on the mining sector underscores its pivotal role in fostering economic resilience and sustainable growth."

a784.speaker: US government / Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) scorecard and programme record
a784.speech: Liberia's qualification for a second compact reflects improvements on the MCC scorecard, which evaluates governance, health, education, economic freedom, and corruption control; the first compact achieved an 8.4% Economic Rate of Return, below MCC's 10% benchmark.

a784.speaker: World Bank and IMF (forecasts)
a784.speech: Forecast Liberia's economy to grow by 5.8% and 5.1%, respectively, in 2025.

a1087.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB) source
a1087.speech: According to AfDB source, the African Development Bank has contributed $1 million from its Special Relief Fund to provide emergency food assistance to flood-affected communities in northeastern Nigeria, in the wake of the devastating floods that hit Borno State in September 2024.

a1087.speaker: David Stevenson, WFP's Country Director in Nigeria
a1087.speech: "The African Development Bank's support is timely and comes as a lifeline for those struggling to feed themselves amidst rising food prices and economic turmoil." ; "Communities which, after years of conflict and violence, started rebuilding their lives were struck by the floods and once again displaced, meaning more and more people cannot support themselves and their families."

a1087.speaker: Abdul Kamara, African Development Bank Director General in Nigeria
a1087.speech: "I hope that this additional funding will mitigate the suffering of vulnerable people on the brink of acute hunger at a time when more Nigerians than ever need humanitarian assistance."

a1087.speaker: Cadre Harmonise food security analysis (November 2024)
a1087.speech: Projects that 33 million people in Nigeria will face food insecurity by August 2025.

a1087.speaker: World Bank Data
a1087.speech: According to World Bank Data, food security continues to be at alarming levels in most low-income countries, particularly in Africa with an estimated 61.6 million food-insecure people in East Africa and nearly 50 million people projected to face food insecurity in Western and Central Africa. Conflicts and climate change continue to be the main driver of food insecurity.

a1087.speaker: World Bank food price inflation data (October 2024-January 2025)
a1087.speech: Shows that inflation higher than 5% is experienced in 73.7% of low-income countries, 52.2% of lower-middle-income countries, 38% of upper-middle-income countries, and 5.6% of high-income countries; in real terms, food price inflation exceeded overall inflation in 56% of the 164 countries where data is available.

a1087.speaker: Agricultural Market Information System (AMIS) Market Monitor, February 2025 edition
a1087.speech: According to it, global prices of AMIS crops (wheat, maize, rice, and soybeans) are currently lower than they were a year ago, with the exception of maize, where international export prices reached a 15-month peak amid supply concerns.

a1087.speaker: 2024 Financing Flows and Food Crises report
a1087.speech: Revealed that, on average, only 3% (USD 6.3 billion) of total development funding is allocated to the food sector - far less than the 33% (USD 10.3 billion) directed toward global humanitarian assistance.

a1087.speaker: World Bank blog post
a1087.speech: Presents five alarming statistics that highlight the urgency of the global food and nutrition security situation and the vital role of data innovations in combating global hunger, noting global hunger affects 733 million people, with rising prices and inefficiencies costing $10 trillion annually.

a1129.speaker: Dr Albertina Shilongo, chief veterinary officer
a1129.speech: Giving an update on the outbreak, said on Friday the source of the FMD infection is suspected to either be due to the contact of cattle with free-roaming buffaloes in the area or smuggling of infected cattle from neighbouring countries: "However, the investigation to ascertain the source of infection is ongoing. The spread of the disease to other villages is due to the movement of livestock to areas in the floodplain in search of better grazing." ; Confirmed emergency vaccination of cattle against FMD has commenced in high-risk areas and it is progressing well ; She announced some control measures to be instituted and will be in force for the next 14 days, including intensive FMD surveillance, movement restriction or ban of all cloven-hoofed animals out, in and through the DMA, restriction of the movement of potentially infectious commodities, suspension of slaughtering of cloven-hoofed animals at local markets and of intake of cattle into the quarantine, and roadblocks and patrol teams around the DMA.

a1129.speaker: Dr Albertina Shilongo, chief veterinary officer
a1129.speech: Updated about the ongoing outbreaks of FMD and Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) in South Africa, saying the South African authority had in June reported that outbreaks of the two diseases have not yet been resolved: "The recent update from the South African Veterinary Authority indicates a continuous spread of FMD within its former FMD-free zone, as the disease has spread to 11 other locations in the Kwazulu Natal Province since May 2021. Similarly, the HPAI infection continues to spread, as a total of 33 new outbreaks were reported across Gauteng, North West, Mpumalanga, Free State, Kwazulu Natal and Eastern Cape provinces since April 2021."

a1129.speaker: South African Veterinary Authority
a1129.speech: Reported in June that outbreaks of FMD and HPAI have not yet been resolved, indicating a continuous spread of FMD within its former FMD-free zone and 33 new HPAI outbreaks since April 2021.

a1184.speaker: Commonwealth summit final communique, Samoa (2024)
a1184.speech: Addressed the issue of reparations, stating: "The time has come for a meaningful, truthful, and respectful conversation towards forging a common future based on equity."

a1200.speaker: U.S. Mission to Nigeria (post on verified X handle, 18 February 2025)
a1200.speech: confirmed that monitoring and evaluation systems are in place to track past assistance provided by the US government. "Comprehensive monitoring and evaluation systems are in place to help verify that U.S. assistance reaches intended recipients," the mission stated.

a1200.speaker: U.S. Mission to Nigeria (statement)
a1200.speech: condemned ongoing violence by Boko Haram and other extremist groups. "The United States condemns the violence and blatant disregard for human life perpetrated by Boko Haram and other terrorist groups in Nigeria and the region" ; "The Secretary of State designated Boko Haram a Foreign Terrorist Organisation on November 14, 2013 to block the organization's assets and fundraising efforts, prosecute individual members, and restrict their travel to the United States." ; "The United States continues to work with Nigeria and regional partners to counter terrorism."

a1200.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a1200.speech: recently claimed that USAID had funded terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram, during the inaugural hearing of the Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency on 14 February 2025. "Who gets some of that money? Does that name ring a bell to anybody in the room? Because your money, your money, $697 million annually, plus the shipments of cash funds in Madrasas, ISIS, Al-Qaeda, Boko Haram, ISIS Khorasan, terrorist training camps. That's what it's funding," Perry said. ; He cited USAID's reported $136 million expenditure to build 120 schools in Pakistan, claiming that there was "zero evidence" of their construction. "You are funding terrorism, and it's coming through USAID. And it's not just Afghanistan, because Pakistan's right next door," Perry alleged.

a1200.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1200.speech: has long called for the closure of USAID and has accused the agency of corruption; his 20 January 2025 decision suspended all foreign aid for 90 days, citing concerns about global destabilisation and misalignment with American interests.

a1200.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1200.speech: has called USAID "a viper's nest of radical-left Marxists who hate America" and alleged that it engages in rogue CIA operations.

a1200.speaker: Department of Government Efficiency (stated mandate)
a1200.speech: His department's mandate includes "dismantling government bureaucracy, slashing excessive regulations, cutting wasteful expenditures, and restructuring federal agencies."

a1237.speaker: Employees and security guards at the locust control center in Qardho
a1237.speech: blame Puntland’s Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation, Mohamed Abdulkadir Salah, widely known as Doonyale, for the wage delays and alleged misappropriation of project funds, reporting that the project has not paid its staff for over eight months.

a1237.speaker: Internal correspondence reviewed by HOL (Hiiraan Online)
a1237.speech: confirms that the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) received formal complaints about unpaid salaries and travel reimbursements covering as early as last August.

a1237.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a1237.speech: advised affected workers to report the matter to the Office of the Auditor General under the Puntland Presidency, which is investigating similar issues; stated it had already conveyed the complaint to the Auditor General “to ensure a comprehensive review and resolution.”

a1237.speaker: Lawmaker of the Puntland regional assembly (unnamed)
a1237.speech: questioned during a session last week whether the government was aware that project staff had not been paid for eight months.

a1237.speaker: Legislators of the Puntland regional assembly
a1237.speech: urged the Minister of Agriculture to respond to the mounting concerns and clarify the status of the program’s finances.

a1237.speaker: Puntland government
a1237.speech: As of publication, has not issued a public response to the allegations.

a1283.speaker: Francisco Tavares, social inclusion specialist on the Cabo Verdean team of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a1283.speech: said the study aims to "realise the potential of young people", to contribute to "increased economic growth" and to "poverty reduction — in Cabo Verde, around 49,000 are outside the labour market, education and training". ; He added that around 2,700 young people with higher education are outside the labour market and that three quarters are in informal occupations. "In Cabo Verde, the majority of young people are outside the productive sector (...). We have qualified and unemployed young people, while there are adults working without qualifications." ; For him, "there is potential to be valued" and the study started "from the premise that the acceleration of youth emigration also results from a misalignment between young people's aspirations and the opportunities the country currently offers".

a1283.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a1283.speech: who presided over the ceremony, expressed the need to "believe in and invest in young people at all levels, so that they can realise their ambitions in Cabo Verde".

a1283.speaker: Afrosondagem study on the quality of democracy and governance in Cabo Verde (released in Praia, December 2024)
a1283.speech: revealed that 64% of Cabo Verdeans are considering emigrating, with the search for work being the main reason.

a1418.speaker: United Nations Charter, Article 2(4)
a1418.speech: States that member states "shall refrain in their international relations from threat or use of force against territorial integrity or political independence of any state..." except in situations in which collective or individual self-defence against an aggression persists.

a1418.speaker: Charter of the Organisation of American States, Article 16
a1418.speech: Proclaims that, "No use of coercive measures of an economic or political character to force the sovereign will of another state and obtain from it advantages of any kind" is permissible.

a1418.speaker: United Nations Declaration on Friendly Relations
a1418.speech: Provided similar sentiments that suggests to outlaw diplomacy, while threats remain indispensable in the intercourse of states, and at times allies.

a1418.speaker: World Politics journal (XIX, No.3, April 1967, p.379)
a1418.speech: Cited as exemplifying the case in point of the effects of International Economic sanctions that were imposed on colonial Rhodesia, reiterating and confirming the failures of sanctions in Zimbabwe.

a1928.speaker: Dr. Getachew Diriba, Senior Advisor to the Minister of Agriculture and Chief Coordinator of the Ethiopian Food System Transformation and Nutrition
a1928.speech: highlighted that Ethiopia was historically among the sub-Saharan African nations most dependent on external assistance, with wheat imports alone costing the country over $1 billion annually.

a1928.speaker: Dr. Ambissa Muleta, Coordinator for the Ethiopian Food System Transition and Healthy Food
a1928.speech: emphasized the role of innovative agricultural practices in this transformation. He pointed to the "Kuta Getem" (cluster farming) method as a key strategy, where farmers collaboratively utilize various mechanized tools to boost their collective productivity.

a1934.speaker: Humanitarian Community in South Sudan
a1934.speech: In 2024, projected that 9.3 million people - 69 per cent of South Sudan's total population of 13.4 million - would require some form of humanitarian assistance in 2025.

a1934.speaker: Body of relief agencies (2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan)
a1934.speech: While launching the 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP), appealed for US$1.7 billion to provide life-saving assistance to 5.4 million people experiencing the most acute needs.

a1934.speaker: South Sudanese advocates and women intellectuals, including Vice President Rebecca Nyandeng
a1934.speech: Speaking at a women's conference in Juba last week, argued that the economic hardships have mostly affected women, who wake up early each day to find something to put food on the table for their children. Some of the advocates called on the government to urgently adopt policies that empower women's socio-economic rights, highlighting their role as the backbone of the country's economy.

a1934.speaker: Rebecca Nyandeng, Vice President for Gender and Youth Cluster of South Sudan
a1934.speech: Acknowledged the strength of women in economic growth and said women's empowerment helps move the country in the right direction. She said women's struggle as caregivers remains unseen by the country, hence leading to the infringement rather than elevation of their economic rights, and strongly called for the adoption of policies that support women at all levels, including businesses and participation in the decision-making process. "South Sudanese women have always been the backbone of our families, our communities, and our economy. You are the strength that holds our nation together." ; "The strength of the women has been hidden. Nobody sees it. And you know that our economy is a foreign-based economy. It has been taken over by foreigners. But few people who are struggling there are women. It is women who wake up before sunrise to sell in the market. We must change this. We must push for policies that uplift women in business, that open doors for them to expand and grow."

a1934.speaker: Dr. Kuyang Harriet, researcher and independent consultant who participated in drafting a position paper on women's socio-economic rights in 2024
a1934.speech: Said the existing bill of rights does not empower women in the country, highlighting significant areas where women are deprived of their rights, including rights to equitable remuneration, healthcare and rights that enable women to own resources. She stated that cultural norms, discriminatory customary practices and stereotyping have backed-up the fading of women's rights in South Sudan. "When you look at our transitional constitution of 2011 as amended, it touches on several socioeconomic rights of everybody in the Bill of Rights, you know, rights to housing, rights to health care, rights to equitable remuneration." ; "So, there are all of these rights that are indeed enshrined for everybody. We say because of culture and customs, stereotypes, and discriminatory customary practices, women are not able to be in a position to enjoy these rights."

a1934.speaker: Deng Kur, legal researcher and advocate for women's empowerment
a1934.speech: Added that inappropriate political will has undermined women's rights and said the women affirmative action enshrined in the transitional constitution should be treated with respect to empower women. "The constitution itself has, to some extent, been abused to an extent that women in South Sudan have felt on many occasions deprived of their constitutional rights. And this comes as a result of a lack of political will, giving very little respect to the rule of law." ; "But if I could say, today we have the transitional constitution, which articulates the equality of everyone, every citizen in South Sudan. We also have the RSS, which articulates that women be represented by 35% in government sectors." ; "All these laws provide a way for representation of women in public life. But then it comes with political will. The political leaders should address themselves to these laws that already exist."

a1934.speaker: Susan Adut, advocate
a1934.speech: Highlighted significant threats that infringed women's rights, citing customs and illiteracy as barriers making women unaware of their rights, and emphasized that advancing women's rights requires scaling up strategies focused on strengthening socio-economic empowerment. "Women have been oppressed here in South Sudan a lot, especially our customs, which are the ones that have really infringed on our rights. And then there is that thing of lack of education. There are a lot of illiterate women who are not aware of their rights." ; "So, I think that advocating for these social and economic rights will make women come up, to empower women who are in the grassroots, who have no idea that they have particular rights which they can advocate for."

a1938.speaker: Local journalists and media analysts (interviews conducted in May 2024 and February 2025)
a1938.speech: Indicate that over 80% of NPE's funding is drawn directly from the state budget.

a1938.speaker: Local journalists interviewed in May 2024 and February 2025
a1938.speech: Affirm that the organization's editorial mission is to promote the policies, positions, and narratives of the state.

a1938.speaker: Ministry of Information of Myanmar
a1938.speech: According to the Ministry of Information, NPE's core mandate is to "focus on publishing newspapers that are in line with the vision of the Ministry of Information to inform, educate and entertain."

a1938.speaker: Maung Maung Ohn, Union Minister for Information
a1938.speech: In July 2025, visited NPE's Yangon offices and urged staff to report with "open eyes and ears," to remain accurate, and to understand state policies thoroughly. He emphasized the Prime Minister's high regard for print media as a source of "trustworthy and reliable information."

a2046.speaker: US officials
a2046.speech: Said most of their home countries had refused to accept them.

a2046.speaker: Rwanda (government)
a2046.speech: Has confirmed discussions on receiving people deported from the US to third countries.

a2046.speaker: US Department of Homeland Security
a2046.speech: Provided a photo to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, showing the men on the plane, their hands and feet shackled.

a2046.speaker: US officials (non-response)
a2046.speech: Officials did not say whether the South Sudanese government had detained them or what their fate would be.

a2046.speaker: US State Department
a2046.speech: Warning against travel to South Sudan because of "crime, kidnapping and armed conflict".

a2046.speaker: Brian Murphy, US district judge in Massachusetts (court ruling)
a2046.speech: Blocked the deportation, having ruled that migrants being deported to third countries must be given notice and a chance to speak with an asylum officer.

a2088.speaker: Dr Edward Omane Boamah, Minister of Defence of Ghana
a2088.speech: Commended the people and government of China for the anniversary celebration; said Ghana had consistently supported China's position on various issues at the UN, particularly China's representation, and its "One China" policy, adding that mutual understanding and respect between the two countries had fostered a strong foundation for their bilateral relations; also said that it was imperative for Ghana and China to continue to nurture and strengthen their partnership, adding that the security landscape in West Africa was complex and multidimensional, with threats from fundamentalists, violent extremists, terrorists and pirates.

a2088.speaker: Dr Edward Omane Boamah, Minister of Defence of Ghana
a2088.speech: Expressed appreciation to the Chinese government for the continuous support to Ghana over the years; mentioned China's "Military Aid Gratis" for the construction of facilities at the National College of Defence Studies and other military projects; said "the projects would significantly enhance the capabilities of our armed forces and ensure we are better equipped to address regional security challenges"; also said that the Chinese government's earlier grant of $50 million stood as a symbol of the enduring partnership between the two countries.

a2088.speaker: Tong Defa, Chinese Ambassador to Ghana
a2088.speech: Said China-Ghana relationship was nurtured about 65 years ago; said the Chinese people had suffered from aggression and wars, and had, therefore, learned the value of peace and the pressing need for development, adding "China has never inflicted such sufferings on any country, and will never do it in the future"; "In today's world, deficits in peace, development, security and governance continue to grow. China will unswervingly follow the path of peaceful development, pursue an independent foreign policy of peace and a national defence policy that is defensive in nature, oppose power politics in all forms, and will never seek hegemony or expansion. The Chinese Military will remain a staunch force in maintaining world peace."

a2088.speaker: Tong Defa, Chinese Ambassador to Ghana
a2088.speech: Said China appreciated Ghana's firm commitment to the One-China principle, respect for national sovereignty and territorial integrity, including its firm opposition to "Taiwan independence"; expressed confidence that under the strong leadership of President Xi Jinping of China and President John Dramani Mahama, the two countries would keep to the aspirations of the founding spirit of their diplomatic ties, uphold mutual respect and win-win cooperation, and also work hand in hand to build an All-Weather China-Africa Community with a shared future for a new era.

a2088.speaker: Colonel Dou Yan, Defence attache at the Chinese Embassy in Ghana
a2088.speech: Said Chinese military had, among other interventions, participated in UN peacekeeping operations, vessel protection operations and international efforts in humanitarian assistance and disaster relief; it had also strengthened international cooperation in arms control and non-proliferation, and played a constructive role in the political settlement of hotspot issues.

a2156.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (press statement)
a2156.speech: Said more than 160,000 people - some with trauma injuries - arrived in northern Upper Nile from war-torn Sudan since mid-December 2024, adding that the ongoing conflict has burdened an already overstretched healthcare system in South Sudan ; said Renk County and its surrounding border villages have become the primary destination for displaced individuals, exacerbating existing health challenges ; said Renk hospital which is vital lifeline for trauma care is struggling to cope with a surge in casualties, registering more than 100 patients a day, as violence intensifies near the Sudan-South Sudan border ; said the response to recent mass casualty incidents has been bolstered by the collaborative efforts of the agency, MSF-Belgium, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), and the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) ; said it has deployed additional makeshift tents, increasing bed capacity by 60.

a2156.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (press statement)
a2156.speech: Said continued humanitarian assistance is critical as the crisis deepens, and stressed the urgent need for sustained funding and resources to support the growing healthcare demands in Renk: "Strengthened coordination and long-term investment in health services are essential to alleviating suffering and ensuring that both displaced populations and host communities receive the care they desperately need."

a2156.speaker: Dr. Ayuel Lual, Medical Director at Renk Hospital
a2156.speech: "The number of patients seeking care in Renk Hospital is increasing daily. We are attending to over 250 outpatients and more than 100 inpatients each day, far exceeding our operational capacity," ; "We are grateful for the timely support from our partners, particularly WHO, whose interventions have been instrumental in keeping the hospital functional."

a2156.speaker: Dr. Humphrey Karamagi, WHO Representative for South Sudan
a2156.speech: Underscored the gravity of the situation: "The scale of displacement is staggering, and health needs have risen dramatically. WHO and partners are ramping up the response by delivering essential medical supplies and expanding health services to new border crossings experiencing a surge in arrivals."

a2167.speaker: Dr Sam Amadi, former chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and Director of Abuja School of Social and Political Thoughts
a2167.speech: Said on the Senate investigation into alleged USAID funding of Boko Haram: "It's a good thing that the National Assembly or the Senate specifically has decided to come and investigate this issue. Everyone just hopes that this will be a real investigation. This is significant... this is not just about Nigeria, it's also about the U.S., as a global power. U.S. has two sides. There is the U.S. that we see, the U.S. promoting democracy, the U.S. supporting material activities, the U.S. with cultural power... There is another U.S., the U.S. of the dark side, where the CIA historically have been involved in some destabilising activities across the world." He said this revelation about USAID presents, maybe in a clearer form, a picture of statecraft and international politics that happens in the name of support or in the name of bilateral relationship or NGOs' support in the world, and that if Nigeria is a serious country it should scrutinise more, build counterintelligence and find out what is happening around it.

a2167.speaker: Dr Sam Amadi, former chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and Director of Abuja School of Social and Political Thoughts
a2167.speech: Said it can help Nigeria develop a more fireproof strategic policy relating to how it deals with nations and understands them and to keeping an eye on the non-profit sector - not in terms of regulating them but in terms of understanding what they are doing. He said: "We have DMI, we have NIA, we have different security intelligence platforms. But I don't really think they are up and doing in intelligence. That's what the scholars call isomorphic mimicry. You create institutions, the forms are there, but the functions are not there." He said that if Nigeria is only now beginning to look at Boko Haram and their activities because of a crisis, a change of government in America and the unpacking of USAID, "then I think it speaks to our lack of preparedness and the lack of real intelligence, and the lack of commitment or even vigor or even awareness and disposition to protect the nation state."

a2167.speaker: Dr Sam Amadi, former chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and Director of Abuja School of Social and Political Thoughts
a2167.speech: On whether the Senate has the political will to unearth the truth: "I don't think it will, but I will be happy for it to be so... for experience, I've never seen a real public investigation, real parliamentary inquiry in recent times in Nigeria. None. So we have to stay on this conversation for like three or four days. They have to have an open session with cameras. They have to have questions. They have to bring the real guys and put them to the sword so that they speak and say what they know and what they don't know. And the outcome of it will be a report that may crystallise in changing how we do national intelligence." He asked how Nigeria cracks mysteries and noted that even when there were signals about who may be involved, including a report about persons funding Boko Haram released by Saudi Arabia or some foreign country, "We didn't follow up on that."

a2167.speaker: Dr Sam Amadi, former chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and Director of Abuja School of Social and Political Thoughts
a2167.speech: Said the U.S. and other world powers may be nefarious countries involved in deep black acts of statecraft and can sponsor regime change, "But at least they are countries that are aware and coherent. The Nigerian problem, and the problem of most African countries, is that they don't even have a coherent state." He said such states may be criminals, dishonest or corrupt "But you know what? They are fiercely focused on preserving their states as an authentic instrument of nationalism or national development," citing Indonesia and Pakistan under the generals as states that were not clean, transparent or accountable but had capacity and commitment to protect themselves, and concluded that "the political will is not some esoteric something. It's just the fact that the leadership in this country hasn't gotten that strong commitment to protect the country above wealth, personal aggrandizement, above personal political projects and it's glaring."

a2167.speaker: Dr Sam Amadi, former chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and Director of Abuja School of Social and Political Thoughts
a2167.speech: On the strength of Nigerian institutions: "The institutions in this country are thoroughly weak. In fact, in the language and the logic of institutions, some of them are no longer institutions." He said that when he was close to power during the Jonathan era he had conversations with top members of that administration who would tell him that members of Boko Haram were in their cabinets: "the helplessness was evident everywhere, that the people inside, with them, cabinet members, had allegiances or some degrees of sympathy and commitment to the Boko Haram project." He explained Peter Evans's concept of embedded autonomy, saying that if state officials are embedded in divisive, incoherent ethnic, religious and ideological tendencies, "then they can't protect the state, they have no protection."

a2167.speaker: Senator Ali Ndume
a2167.speech: Reportedly said the funding of the sect (Boko Haram) is a mystery.

a2167.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman (referenced in interviewer's question)
a2167.speech: In his address he talked not just about Nigeria but about Palestine, Afghanistan and several other countries in relation to alleged USAID funding.

a2266.speaker: African Briefing (media report, "Tradition is Africa's future")
a2266.speech: "in a stirring speech before Ghana's National House of Chiefs in Kumasi this week, His Majesty King Mswati III made an impassioned case for the preservation and integration of traditional leadership into modern governance." ; "Chieftaincy is not a symbol but a system."

a2266.speaker: King Mswati III (Ingwenyama) of Eswatini, speaking at Ghana's National House of Chiefs in Kumasi
a2266.speech: "Standing before Ghana's top traditional leaders, King Mswati III declared that while elected governments rotate every five years, traditional leadership remains a permanent institution grounded in community, ancestry and trust. Governments come and go, but traditional leadership never goes."

a2266.speaker: King Mswati III (Ingwenyama) of Eswatini
a2266.speech: Announced the establishment of a formal Council of Chiefs; "The king drew comparison between Ghana's House of Chiefs and Eswatini Tinkhundla Governance Model, where chiefs are empowered to mediate, preserve heritage and shape community life. These structures, he argued, are not remains from the past, but vital governance pillars in the present. In Eswatini, this is not only cherished, but enshrined in our Constitution and he said, chiefs were the foundation of our monarchy, ensuring the were people's voices are heard." ; Revealed that Eswatini is establishing a formal council of Chiefs to advise the state on tradition, custom and cultural preservation; an effort to institutionalise indigenous wisdom in national decision making.

a2266.speaker: 2005 Constitution of the Kingdom of Eswatini, Section 251(1)
a2266.speech: "There shall be a council of chiefs which shall be comprised of twelve chiefs drawn from the four regions of the kingdom appointed by Ingwenyama on rotational basis."

a2266.speaker: Kings and queens of African kingdoms (Royal Chamber of the State of African Diaspora pilot research, Nigeria, Liberia, Angola, Kongo and South Africa)
a2266.speech: What emerged during these conversations with kings and queens is that African kingdoms continue practicing their indigenous governance, spirituality, diplomacy and cultural technologies, which are currently marginalised by the local or national governments that control land, leaving chiefs with limited power.

a2364.speaker: Leonidas Ndaruzaniye, Governor of Ngozi province
a2364.speech: In his address, called on the administrative officials of Gashikanwa to strengthen unity, to maintain peace and security, to mobilise the population to increase production and to be mediators of the people; recalled the essential contribution of administrative officials in strengthening unity and unifying the people, that nothing can separate or divide the people, and urged them to serve as models in strengthening unity, to unite, to reconcile and to encourage the population to develop.

a2364.speaker: Leonidas Ndaruzaniye, Governor of Ngozi province
a2364.speech: Recalling the imminence of the elections, recommended that the administrative officials strengthen security, avoid rumours and disinformation, and inform those responsible for security in case of suspicion of anything that could cause insecurity.

a2364.speaker: Leonidas Ndaruzaniye, Governor of Ngozi province
a2364.speech: Encouraged the population of Gashikanwa commune for the step taken in development, and reassured farmers that the government is preparing to buy maize, inviting them to preserve their harvest better and to avoid selling it at a low price.

a2364.speaker: Ferdinand Habimana, provincial secretary of the ruling party in the new province of Butanyerera
a2364.speech: Called on the population of Gashikanwa commune to prepare better for the coming elections, to be guided by solidarity despite their diversity of political ideologies, and to apply themselves to activities aimed at the development of households and of the country in general; called on the population to develop export crops, including avocados and coffee.

a2427.speaker: Mohamed Yari, First Deputy Mayor of Parakou
a2427.speech: Said that this activity, planned within the framework of the project, offers religious leaders the opportunity to better absorb their role in social cohesion and peacebuilding within their communities, their towns and the nation as a whole.

a2427.speaker: Emilienne Cyuzuzo, Programme Director at Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a2427.speech: Assures that, with these resulting actions, the workshop will allow the sharing of knowledge and practices in religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence.

a2427.speaker: Reverend Alphonse Kinkponhoué, President of the UEEB
a2427.speech: Presented the first workshop communication, entitled “The Christian religion and social cohesion.”

a2437.speaker: Mozambican commercial banks (announcement)
a2437.speech: On Friday announced the availability of 10 billion meticais (156.5 million US dollars at the current exchange rate) aimed at funding companies affected by post-election rioting, looting and destruction, accessible at an interest rate of 15 percent, with each bank analysing company risk based on its internal procedures.

a2437.speaker: Teotónio Comiche, Chairperson of the Association of Mozambican Banks
a2437.speech: Said the loans and their interest must be repaid within 12 months, “while for capital investments, the term is five years”; said that in order to gain access to the credit, the banks will have to request guarantees from the companies and the credit will be available from 1 March to 30 September.

a2437.speaker: Confederation of Mozambican Business Associations (CTA)
a2437.speech: Once again called on the government to guarantee security, so that businesses may feel safe to operate, as mass protests, characterized by rioting, looting and destruction, are continuing in some parts of the country ; according to CTA data, about 900 companies have been affected by the post-election rioting, which corresponds to the loss of 17,000 jobs.

a2437.speaker: Carla Louveira, Mozambican Finance Minister
a2437.speech: Said the government is working with the banks to establish long-term measures for this credit line: “The government is aware of the concerns about people’s safety, as well as private and public property, and how this affects investment and day-to-day economic activities. We are continuing to work towards maintaining law and order, restoring investment confidence and improving our business environment.”

a2472.speaker: Mumba Kalifungwa, Managing Director, Absa Bank Uganda
a2472.speech: Expressed sympathies about the disaster and spoke of the bank's solidarity with those affected: "We would like to identify with the affected families and lend a helping hand after this unfortunate incident, under our commitment of being a force for good within the communities in which we operate. I call upon other private sector players and individuals to support in whatever way they are able to, in the wake of human suffering brought by this tragedy."

a2472.speaker: Robert Kwesiga, Secretary General, Uganda Red Cross Society
a2472.speech: Appreciated Absa Bank leadership for coming through in a timely manner to support the affected families: "I want to thank my brother Mumba and his entire team at Absa for being people focused. Coming through at such a time is a big expression of your sense of humanity towards the community. These may not even be your bank customers, but your level of commitment and response, shows how compassionate you are towards the people. Thank you very much."

a2472.speaker: Robert Kwesiga, Secretary General, Uganda Red Cross Society
a2472.speech: Mentioned that Uganda Red Cross has been on ground since Saturday when the incident happened and the team has been working tirelessly to save lives, and also ensure that the deceased are accorded the decency that they deserve ; "We have teams on the ground as we conduct search and rescue / recovery operations and provide relief support to the most affected people. The affected families need relief food aid and non-food relief items to enable them cope through the emergency phase. Uganda Red Cross seeks support of partners to be able to offer more timely and meaningful humanitarian assistance to the affected families. This support from Absa Bank will go a long way in relieving human suffering, pain, stress and trauma, to those in need."

a2472.speaker: Uganda Red Cross Society
a2472.speech: According to the Uganda Red Cross, the donation will fund the purchase of essential home shelter kits that will provide temporary shelter and basic household essentials for over 200 families.

a2596.speaker: Ecobank Uganda
a2596.speech: Urged Ugandans to embrace a stronger culture of giving to support community-led initiatives as foreign aid continues to decline, making the appeal while donating to Angel’s Centre for Children with Special Needs.

a2621.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Malawi Minister of Health
a2621.speech: Has assured Malawians that the country has sufficient stocks of HIV/AIDS drugs to last for at least 11 months, dismissing fears that the suspension of USAID funding could disrupt treatment and care ; “We have continued to provide services as usual. Where USAID has withdrawn staff, we have deployed our own health workers to fill the gaps” ; emphasized that Malawi has adequate stocks to manage HIV/AIDS treatment for the next 11 months, adding that the government is utilizing the Health Sector Joint Fund—supported by Germany, Norway, and the United Kingdom—to bridge financial shortfalls left by USAID’s funding suspension.

a2621.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Malawi Minister of Health
a2621.speech: Reassured the public not to panic, stating that the government is actively engaging other development partners to ensure continuity in the health sector. However, she did not provide specific details on how the government sourced the additional healthcare workers replacing those previously supported by U.S. funding.

a2621.speaker: 74th ECSA-HC Health Ministers Conference
a2621.speech: The conference downplayed the potential impact of the USAID funding suspension, citing ECSA-HC’s cost-effective operational model.

a2621.speaker: Sibusiso Sibandze, ECSA-HC Acting Director-General
a2621.speech: Stressed that while USAID funding has been valuable, the organization implements its activities efficiently: “Even with the funding withdrawal, we are confident in our ability to continue supporting member states.”

a2621.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice-President of Malawi
a2621.speech: Urged member states to prioritize health data integration and adopt innovative financing strategies to strengthen regional health systems.

a2643.speaker: Patrice Lumumba (quoted epigraph)
a2643.speech: “I prefer to die with my head unbowed, my faith unshakeable and with profound trust in the destiny of my country, rather than live under subjection and disregarding sacred principles. History will one day have its say, but it will not be the history that is taught in Brussels, Paris, Washington or in the United Nations. But the history which will be taught in the countries freed from imperialism and its puppets.”

a2643.speaker: Declaration adopted following the second Russia-Africa summit in St Petersburg (document)
a2643.speech: Africa is proclaimed as playing an “increasing global role and influence as one of the key pillars of a multipolar world.”

a2643.speaker: Experts (demographic projections)
a2643.speech: Estimate that by 2050, the continent’s population could reach 2.5 billion, meaning one in four people on Earth will be African.

a2643.speaker: Informed Russian experts
a2643.speech: According to informed Russian experts, African countries “support each other on the global stage and adopt common positions on many current international issues.”

a2643.speaker: African experts
a2643.speech: Lament that the West is unwilling “to recognize the right of the continent’s countries to set their own agenda” and that its policy toward opponents amounts to “punishing them for having their own interests”; some Africans openly call on “the EU and other U.S. allies not to impose their way of life and values on those who do not wish it.”

a2643.speaker: African experts (on colonialism)
a2643.speech: Believe that the foundations of the continent’s complex underdevelopment and the conflicts arising from territorial and ethno-religious divisions were largely laid by the predatory policies of colonizers.

a2643.speaker: African experts (on Western aid)
a2643.speech: Lament that, for example, the US Agency for International Development (USAID) predominantly promotes a political agenda rooted in neoliberal globalist ideology, prioritizing activities in Africa such as promoting “democracy, supporting civil society, and assisting in leadership elections.”

a2643.speaker: Bernard Dadie, poet (Cote d'Ivoire) (quoted epigraph)
a2643.speech: “God deliver us from Europe, which cares about our freedom.”

a2643.speaker: Bai T. Moore, Liberian poet
a2643.speech: Wrote in the 1950s, “Civilization is in full swing – gold and diamonds are sent to Europe.”

a2643.speaker: Ngugi wa Thiong'o, Kenyan writer
a2643.speech: Aptly noted that the West’s struggle for Africa revolves around “access to local resources.”

a2643.speaker: African political analysts
a2643.speech: Rightly point out, “The West benefits from a system in which any so-called progress is driven primarily by multinational corporations and does not translate into development.”

a2643.speaker: International Coffee Organization (estimate)
a2643.speech: Estimates the annual turnover of the global coffee market at $460 billion.

a2643.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a2643.speech: Pointed out that African nations are “offered modern tools and technologies, but they cannot afford them... and no one provides funding. Instead, they are forced to depend on Western technologies and loans. These loans come with horrific conditions and are impossible to repay. This is yet another tool of neo-colonialism.”

a2643.speaker: African political scientists (on the UN)
a2643.speech: According to African political scientists, the UN, despite operating five peacekeeping missions in Africa, has demonstrated a chronic inability to improve security.

a2643.speaker: Young African experts
a2643.speech: Rightly argue that “escaping subjugation begins with decolonizing the mind.”

a2643.speaker: Some Western scholars
a2643.speech: Reluctantly admit that “African countries need to be understood and respected”; they worry that Russia “leverages Africa’s frustration with inadequate representation in the global economy and governance,” and hold that “the continent will not accept moralizing lectures.”

a2643.speaker: African historians
a2643.speech: Adhere to the principle that “Only formulas developed by Africans themselves, not imposed from outside, will work on the continent.”

a2643.speaker: Experts on Africa
a2643.speech: Emphasize that, under these new conditions, the continent must focus on developing its own institutions and deepening intra-African cooperation based on mutual benefit rather than dependency.

a2643.speaker: UN General Assembly resolution 'Eradication of Colonialism in All Its Forms and Manifestations' (December 2024) (document)
a2643.speech: Aims to ensure full implementation of the 1960 Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples, and proposes designating December 14 as the International Day for the Eradication of Colonialism in All Its Forms and Manifestations.

a2643.speaker: African politicians and experts
a2643.speech: Highly value the potential of BRICS, viewing it as a driver for building a new and fair international order, and a cornerstone of the emerging architecture of international relations that is replacing unipolar mechanisms.

a2643.speaker: Russian political analysts
a2643.speech: Emphasize that the expansion of BRICS, including the addition of Egypt and Ethiopia, is “a visible testament to the world’s movement toward multipolarity.”

a2643.speaker: Sergey Lavrov, Russian Foreign Minister
a2643.speech: Aptly noted, “We are witnessing Africa’s second awakening, this time from neo-colonial oppression and practices that hinder its development.”

a2643.speaker: Somali proverb (quoted epigraph)
a2643.speech: “God grant us rain or Russians.”

a2643.speaker: Concept of the Foreign Policy of the Russian Federation (document)
a2643.speech: Notes that the country intends to support the African continent “as a distinctive and influential center of world development.”

a2643.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President (on Russia-Africa ties)
a2643.speech: According to Vladimir Putin, cooperation with African states is one of the enduring priorities of Russia’s foreign policy ; He has stated: “In the history of our relations with the African continent, there has never been any shadow – never. We have never exploited African peoples, nor have we engaged in anything inhumane on the African continent. On the contrary, we have always supported Africa and Africans in their struggle for independence, sovereignty, and the creation of basic conditions for economic development.”

a2643.speaker: Declaration of the Russia-Africa summit (document)
a2643.speech: Highlights the historically established and time-tested friendly ties between the Russian Federation and African states, based on mutual respect, trust, and a tradition of cooperative struggle for the eradication of colonialism and the establishment of independence for African countries.

a2643.speaker: Joint statement issued following the 2024 Sochi Ministerial Conference (document)
a2643.speech: Emphasizes “the responsibility of the Russian Federation and African states to promote the formation of a fair and stable world order based on the principles of sovereign equality of states, non-interference in their internal affairs, and respect for sovereignty.”

a2643.speaker: African political scientists (on Russia)
a2643.speech: Note that, unlike former colonial powers, Russia has historically aimed to address real problems without pursuing selfish interests.

a2643.speaker: African experts (on Russia's military operation in Ukraine)
a2643.speech: Draw a connection between Russia’s special military operation in Ukraine and the successes of African nations in their struggle for independence, noting that “the course of Russia’s confrontation with the West influences the sentiments of nationally-oriented, sovereign forces in the region.”

a2643.speaker: Local analysts
a2643.speech: Note that “after the failure of France and UN peacekeeping forces in Africa, Russia has emerged as a reliable partner, accomplishing in a few months what international contingents failed to do for years.”

a2643.speaker: Individuals who built their careers in diplomacy in the 1990s and 2000s (anonymous)
a2643.speech: Occasionally argue that “few would want to work in Africa, given its harsher climate and limited medical facilities compared to Europe.”

a2643.speaker: Scholars of Africa
a2643.speech: Rightly point out that this prospect has a direct impact on the fate of multipolarity.

a2678.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2678.speech: Acknowledged this was a long statement and justified it: "I have taken long deliberately because this is a House of records and I want it to be on record that this is what I have delivered for the Malawian people in the four years that I have been President, and I believe that I am at peace with God and I have enough trust in the Malawian people that they are fair minded enough to judge my performance as President by what I have done, not by what other politicians say about me or by the disasters that have befallen us as a nation and subjected us to a season of pain that we must have the strength to endure and overcome, and I believe that overcome we will."

a2678.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2678.speech: Said he had delivered so much to the people of various districts in their season of sacrificial pain and he expects to deliver even more by 2030 ; at the end of each district presentation, told the voters to be ready to hear other parties offering to take the districts backward, while he is ready to continue taking the developments forward ; appealed to registered voters in each district to vote for continued development in the September elections.

a2678.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2678.speech: On Thyolo, home district of former presidents Bingu wa Mutharika and Peter Mutharika: "I believe it is safe to say that nowhere is the false claim that I have done nothing for Malawians repeated by dishonest politicians than in Thyolo, so today I thank the Lord for the opportunity to set the record straight."

a2678.speaker: George Chaponda, Leader of Opposition
a2678.speech: Described it as a mere campaign speech and not a Sona ; according to Chaponda, the address fell short of outlining what plans the President has for Malawi moving forward in the wake of deteriorating economic environment.

a2678.speaker: Bertha Chikadza, President of the Economics Association of Malawi
a2678.speech: Said her organisation also expected to hear a lot on the strategies the government has to turnaround the flailing economy: "So at this point we just need those opinions, those words to tell us that things are going to turn around, the economy is going to be on track and so on and so forth. So we wanted that to come out strongly."

a2678.speaker: Thomas Munthali, outgoing Director General of the National Planning Commission
a2678.speech: Said what the President wanted to present was that there is a lot of development taking place at the district level: "You remember that he was mentioning all the members of Parliament in a particular district meaning that the developments that have taken place is not just because of the government of the day but also the efforts of other political parties that are playing a role, including the non-state actors that are working there." ; said, however, that he had hoped Chakwera would highlight how the government intends to sustain those developments.

a2678.speaker: Daisy Kambalame, Chief Executive Officer of the Malawi Confederation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MCCCI)
a2678.speech: Said the breaking down of developments in the districts highlighted the opportunities available at district level: "I think the key thing is to now have a conversation on what we do now. How do we build on that foundation to look at creating opportunities for real partnerships so that the infrastructure developments he was talking about starts bearing fruits?"

a2731.speaker: Adugna Debela, Director-General of the Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority
a2731.speech: “Ethiopia’s value added coffee export is less than two percent and almost all export goes outside Africa,” adding that Ethiopia should work on improving its coffee export law for African countries ; “This is against the government’s attempt to lower domestic coffee consumption in order to have more coffee beans for export.”

a2731.speaker: Adugna Debela, Director-General of the Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority
a2731.speech: According to the director, the Authority is working to expand its market access to African countries by value addition of its coffee bean ; Ethiopia is still a major producing country of high-value coffee and the government is targeting African countries as alternative coffee export destinations as the price in global market fluctuates.

a2731.speaker: Denis Sedieu, chief economist at the International Coffee Organization (ICO)
a2731.speech: “The increasing trend in coffee consumption in African countries and opening opportunities to trade within African countries will benefit coffee growing farmers and stabilize coffee prices.”

a2731.speaker: Coffee export data 2017/18 (Ethiopian export statistics)
a2731.speech: Based on the coffee export data 2017/18, the principal export markets for Ethiopian coffee were Germany, Saudi Arabia, United States, Belgium, Sudan and Italy, registering a record of 917 million USD that makes coffee the most important export for the country, accounting for about 34 percent of the value of all exports.

a2873.speaker: Francis Bacon (quoted)
a2873.speech: Said in his own way that there are “some books to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested”

a2873.speaker: John Perkins, author of 'Confessions of an Economic Hit Man', former Economic Hit Man
a2873.speech: Said that it was very difficult for him to publish the book: at first he could not get daring publishers, and he did not accept the advice to fictionalize it

a2873.speaker: A man at a publishing house owned by a powerful international corporation
a2873.speech: Read the draft and said it was “a riveting story that needs to be told”, but fearing bad reactions from his big bosses, advised Perkins to fictionalize it

a2873.speaker: A reader of the book (quoted)
a2873.speech: “Perkins reveals shocking details of how United States Government and corporate America work hand in hand in maintaining a dominating role in international affairs by using greed and corruption to inhibit foreign governments from economic development”

a2873.speaker: John Perkins, author of 'Confessions of an Economic Hit Man'
a2873.speech: Tells us that EHMs are highly paid professionals who cheat countries around the globe out of trillions of dollars, funnelling money from the World Bank, the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), and other foreign “aid” organizations into the coffers of huge corporations and the pockets of a few wealthy families who control the planet's natural resources

a2873.speaker: Perkins's immediate boss (quoted in the book)
a2873.speech: Told Perkins about his responsibilities: “[You] are paid to cheat countries around the globe out of billions of dollars. A large part of your job is to encourage world leaders to become part of a vast network that promotes U.S. commercial interests. In the end, those leaders become ensnared in a web of debt that ensures their loyalty. We can draw on them whenever we desire – to satisfy our political, economic, or military needs. In return, these leaders bolster their political positions by bringing industrial parks, power plants, and airports to their people. Meanwhile, the owners of U.S. engineering and construction companies become very wealthy”

a2873.speaker: John Perkins, author of 'Confessions of an Economic Hit Man'
a2873.speech: Recounts in his book: “Like our counterparts in the Mafia, EHMs provide favors. These take the form of loans to develop infrastructure – electric generating plants, high ways, ports, air ports, or industrial parks”, and that the loan given by the World Bank “never leaves the United States; it is simply transferred from banking offices in Washington to engineering offices in New York, Houston, or San Francisco” ; “When this happens, then like the Mafia we demand our pound of flesh. This often includes one or more of the following: control over United Nations votes, the installations of military bases, or access to precious resources such as oil...” and “the global empire demands its pounds of flesh in the form of oil concessions”

a2873.speaker: John Perkins, author of 'Confessions of an Economic Hit Man'
a2873.speech: Writes of Ecuador's president: “Roldos warned all foreign interests, including but not limited to oil companies, that unless they implemented plans that would help Ecuador's people, they would be forced to leave his country. He delivered a major speech at the Atahualpa Olympic Stadium in Quito and then headed off to a small community in southern Ecuador. He died there in a fiery airplane crash on May 24, 1981.” ; “Omar Torrijos... confessed to having nightmares about his own assassination; he saw himself dropping from the sky in a gigantic fireball. It was prophetic... Two months after Roldos's death, Omar Torrijos's nightmare came true; he died in a plane crash. There was a bomb in the small plane in which he was flying... It was July 31, 1981.”

a2873.speaker: John Perkins, author of 'Confessions of an Economic Hit Man'
a2873.speech: Writes that “[f]or every $100 of crude oil taken from Ecuadorian rain forest, the [American] oil companies receive $75. Of the remaining $25, three-quarter must go to paying off the foreign dept. Most of the reminder covers military and other government expenses – which leaves about $2.50 for health, education, and programs aimed at helping the poor. Thus, out of every $100 worth oil torn from the Amazon, less than $3 goes to the people who need the money most”

a2873.speaker: John Perkins, author of 'Confessions of an Economic Hit Man'
a2873.speech: Expressing the atrocious acts in Panama, says: “The U.S. army had prohibited the press, the Red Cross and other outside observers from entering the heavily bombarded areas [of Panama] for three days, while soldiers incinerated and buried the causalities”

a3283.speaker: Justin Saidi, Chief Secretary to the Government of Malawi (statement)
a3283.speech: Says the appointments are with immediate effect, which have been done in the powers conferred upon the President under Section 94(1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Malawi.

a3384.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a3384.speech: Stated this Tuesday that two million Mozambicans are facing food insecurity, of whom 148,000 require “urgent humanitarian assistance”.

a3384.speaker: Inócencio Impissa, Council of Ministers spokesperson (Mozambique)
a3384.speech: Released preliminary data from the food security assessment in the post-rainy season period, conducted in March and April among 11 million citizens in 66 districts: “Of the 11 million citizens reached, 5.2 million have satisfactory levels of food security, four million are able to feed themselves, and two million Mozambicans are experiencing food insecurity” ; added that at least 148,000 people are in an emergency situation, “requiring urgent humanitarian assistance” ; “The government, through the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) and partners, is working to meet the needs of these households, and support in terms of agricultural inputs and tools is also underway for the 2025-26 agricultural season.”

a3384.speaker: Cândido Ampute, southern regional director of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD)
a3384.speech: Said on August 7: “In Mozambique, […] it is estimated that approximately 2.3 million people could face acute food insecurity by the end of the 2024/2025 season” ; said El Niño had a significant impact on agriculture and “consequently on food insecurity”, particularly in central parts of Mozambique.

a3384.speaker: National Institute of Statistics (Mozambique)
a3384.speech: According to its data, extreme events caused at least 1,016 deaths in Mozambique between 2019 and 2023, affecting approximately 4.9 million people.

a3384.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report, February
a3384.speech: Estimated that approximately 3.3 million people would face food insecurity due to the impacts of climate shocks and the armed insurgency in Mozambique.

a3384.speaker: United Nations
a3384.speech: Estimated at the time that food insecurity worsened by El Niño had reached “unprecedented levels” in Mozambique, threatening nearly five million people, amid a drought and a lack of international funding for on-the-ground support.

a3384.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a3384.speech: Says the findings stem from an analysis of agricultural activity and food insecurity, indicating that it “has reached unprecedented levels in Mozambique,” with a total of 4,890,232 people threatened by food insecurity by the end of the campaign, which concluded in March ; OCHA launched an appeal in 2024 for US$222 million (€213 million) in international support to combat the effects of the drought in Mozambique, but acknowledges that it faces “a significant funding gap,” having raised only US$28.7 million (€27.5 million), equivalent to 13% of the needs identified.

a3653.speaker: Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, Vice President of Ghana and New Patriotic Party (NPP) presidential candidate
a3653.speech: Has reiterated his commitment to providing incentives to churches and faith-based organizations in recognition of their significant contributions to national development; noted that despite their contributions these groups currently do not receive the same incentives that are extended to foreign development partners; pledged to offer incentives including waivers on special equipment and machinery used for development projects ; “I want to collaborate with the churches and Islamic institutions. When you look at the volume of development work in this country, they contribute a lot. They build schools and hospitals, yet the government does not give them incentives” ; “When foreign aid organisations come here for development, they are classified as development partners and receive certain benefits, such as waivers on duties for materials used in building schools or churches. But when churches or Islamic institutions bring in similar materials, they are asked to pay duties. I want to change that” ; “I want to reclassify churches and faith-based institutions as development partners, so they can enjoy the same incentives extended to foreign development partners. When they bring in equipment for schools and hospitals, they will also be exempt from duties. This will significantly aid the development of our country.”

a3653.speaker: Representatives of the religious groups (clergy and imams)
a3653.speech: Expressed their excitement at the prospect of receiving such support; in previous visits, both clergy and imams in various communities have also welcomed the initiative, recognising its potential to further enhance the work of religious institutions in national development.

a3773.speaker: Philippe Kourouma, author, singer-songwriter and Director General of SONOGUI (Sonorities of Guinea)
a3773.speech: On how he came into music: "I have been hooked on music since primary school... At first I had opted for recitations. Suddenly one day I changed direction, and I sang instead of reciting. My voice pleased the teacher, and he spotted me."
