a7039.speaker: Ronald Münch, German ambassador to Mozambique
a7039.speech: Speaking to reporters during the 60th edition of the Maputo International Fair (FACIM 2025), said the Zambezi Valley Agency brings together all the potential of the central region, in the sectors of agribusiness, tourism, fishing and sustainable forestry: “We already know that the agency plays a very important role in the development of various sectors, and we are very pleased that the German government, through its development agencies, is a partner of the Zambezi Agency, because our commitment is to facilitate the development of various sectors, especially agriculture, for the well-being of the people” ; explained that the “what we now have, in the planning stage, is a large-scale project to finance the projects of the Zambezi Agency and the businesses. These projects begin with the planning of an idea, through the development of small businesses, certification for export, and even the export of these projects.” ; “Germany will continue supporting the Zambezi Valley Development Agency through its financing lines.”

a7337.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a7337.speech: "Our elections are over; it was tough, it was complicated, and everybody saw what happened, but now we have a President-elect in the capacity of Dr. Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah. She will have time to organise her things because, according to our rules, having started from the year we gained our independence, we had elections in November 1989, and we needed 3 months to draft the Constitution, and that is why our independence is in March, and because of that we always have elections in November. But the assumption of power is in March. Nevertheless, we are comfortable now that when the dust has settled, everybody will accept what we have gotten from the people of Namibia. We have solid bilateral relations. We are benefiting from PEPFAR in terms of health, AGOA in terms of trade, YALI, and the Peace Corps."

a7337.speaker: Randy Berry, US Ambassador to Namibia
a7337.speech: Informed President Mbumba: "I also had a chance to discuss with the President how much I believe that is intensifying rapidly. I think all of the elements for closer relationships for increased coordination and collaboration are based on those very items, and when you are talking about democracies, democracies are driven by the rule of law, driven by institutions, and they are driven by elections, and those bring us together in terms of making sure that people's voices are heard. One area where I see a great deal of hope is expanding the economic situation; obviously, Namibians want opportunities; they want an economy that is thriving. We have seen a significant increase in private-sector investment from US firms here."

a7337.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia, and Randy Berry, US Ambassador to Namibia
a7337.speech: Reaffirmed that the bilateral ties between Namibia and the USA would continue to remain stable, anchored on democratic principles, in light of the general elections that took place in both countries.

a7363.speaker: World Inequality Report 2018
a7363.speech: According to the recently released World Inequality Report 2018, in the United States the share of national income claimed by the top 1% of the population rose from 11% in 1980 to 20% in 2014, compared to just 13% for the entire bottom half of the population; qualitatively similar, though less pronounced, trends characterize other major countries such as France, Germany, and the United Kingdom.

a7363.speaker: Xavier Sala-i-Martin, Columbia University
a7363.speech: Pointed out in 2002 and 2006 that even as inequality has risen in nearly every country, inequality across countries has decreased, owing largely to the success of developing countries like China and India in raising their per capita incomes since the 1980s.

a7363.speaker: Adam Smith and David Ricardo
a7363.speech: Made the case that trade would normally benefit both partners, by enabling each to take advantage of their comparative advantages.

a7363.speaker: Heckscher-Ohlin-Stolper-Samuelson (HO-SS) trade theory
a7363.speech: Predicted that international trade would benefit the abundant factor of production (in rich countries, the owners of capital) and hurt the scarce factor of production (in rich countries, unskilled labor); workers could command higher wages if they did not have to compete against abundant labor in poorer countries.

a7363.speaker: Paul Krugman and Elhanan Helpman
a7363.speech: Introduced the previously neglected elements of imperfect competition and increasing returns to scale.

a7363.speaker: Marc Melitz
a7363.speech: Showed in 2003 how trade could shift resources from low-productivity to high-productivity firms.

a7363.speaker: Pinelopi Goldberg and Nina Pavcnik
a7363.speech: Reported in 2007 that the expectation that trade would reduce inequality in the countries with the most unskilled workers, because their services are in greater demand in an integrated world market, has not been borne out: "There is overwhelming evidence," they write, "that less-skilled workers in developing countries are generally not better off, at least not relative to workers with higher skill or education levels."

a7363.speaker: Branko Milanovic and Lyn Squire
a7363.speech: Also found, in 2007, that tariff reduction is associated with higher inequality in poor countries.

a7412.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde
a7412.speech: Announced at the beginning of September that it expects to present the projects to be financed, in an amount that is not yet known, within two years ; the delegation's agenda released by the Government includes only two meetings, on Wednesday: one with the Deputy Prime Minister responsible for Finance and the Digital Economy, Olavo Correia, and another with the Prime Minister, Ulisses Correia e Silva.

a7412.speaker: Christopher Broughton (biographical note)
a7412.speech: According to his biographical note, Christopher Broughton is a project-management professional and a member of the Council on Foreign Relations; he is fluent in French and Spanish and has some knowledge of Hindi, Urdu and Portuguese.

a7457.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a7457.speech: According to the NGO, Donald Trump's political career "was in part defined by a propensity to spread falsehoods", having made, over the course of his first term, "more than 30,000 false or misleading statements, a volume of inaccuracy without equal in American history", including the consistent denial of the 2020 election results.

a7457.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7457.speech: In February asserted that Ukraine "should never have started" the war ; labelled his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodymyr Zelensky, a "dictator" and accused him of refusing to hold elections ; falsely asserted that Zelensky had only 4% popular approval ; claimed that the US had spent 350 billion dollars on aid to Ukraine, or 200 billion more than Europe.

a7457.speaker: Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KIIS) polls
a7457.speech: Showed that, in February, 57% of Ukrainians trusted Zelensky.

a7457.speaker: Kiel Institute, German think tank tracking aid to Ukraine (data)
a7457.speech: Indicated that, by the end of 2024, the US had committed about 124 billion dollars, while the EU and individual European countries had collectively given far more military, financial and humanitarian aid to Kyiv: around 228 billion euros (258 billion dollars).

a7457.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7457.speech: In January asserted that his administration had "identified and prevented 50 million dollars from being sent to Gaza to buy condoms for [the Palestinian Islamist movement] Hamas" ; made various false or unfounded allegations about USAID as part of the campaign to dismantle the agency and drastically reduce US foreign aid, asserting without presenting evidence that "billions of dollars were stolen from USAID" and used as bribes so that the press would create stories favourable to the Democrats.

a7457.speaker: The New York Times
a7457.speech: Identified millions of dollars in federal grants awarded to prevent sexually transmitted diseases in the Mozambican province of Gaza, and not in the Palestinian territory.

a7457.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7457.speech: In the first address of the year before Congress, in March, declared that he had "inherited from the last Government an economic catastrophe and an inflationary nightmare" ; last week falsely asserted that food prices are "falling and coming down".

a7457.speaker: CNN International (fact-check)
a7457.speech: A fact-check by the international television channel CNN found that food prices continued to rise, even before Trump imposed almost global tariffs of 10% earlier this month ; CNN International stressed that, besides the fact that it is US importers who make the tariff payments, the US has collected billions of dollars in customs duties on Chinese imports for years.

a7457.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7457.speech: Repeated this month the frequent false claim that, before his first Presidency (2017-2021), China "never paid 10 cents to any other President" in tariffs.
